title: Assessing Blood Pressure Variability in a Healthy Adult Population During Transcutaneous Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation With the Zeus Sleep Device
official: Assessing Blood Pressure Variability in a Healthy Adult Population During Transcutaneous Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation With the Zeus Sleep Device
summary:
Transcutaneous hypoglossal nerve stimulation is an emerging treatment option for Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA), a sleep condition where breathing is repeatedly limited. The standard treatment for OSA is not always well tolerated therefore, more alternatives are needed.

Transcutaneous hypoglossal nerve stimulation uses a device, such as Zeus, which sticks underneath the chin to deliver electrical pulses during sleep. These pulses stimulate the hypoglossal nerve to prevent the tongue from relaxing and blocking the airway.

Device placement is important for specific nerve targeting; however, its proximity is close to receptors involved in blood pressure regulation. Whilst current research indicates that transcutaneous stimulation is unlikely to increase blood pressure, OSA patients have an increased risk of developing high blood pressure, therefore treatment options should not make this worse. Further research to understand the impact of transcutaneous hypoglossal nerve stimulation on blood pressure is therefore needed. In this study, the blood pressure of participants will be measured whilst they wear the Zeus sleep device. It is expected that blood pressure will either decrease or remain constant in line with current research. Findings could facilitate improved confidence in device use for OSA treatment and provide patients with alternative treatment options.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Adults aged 18 or older
2. Either biological sex
3. Healthy volunteers
4. Able to provide informed consent
5. No contraindications to hypoglossal nerve stimulation using the Zeus device
6. BMI \>18.5 and \<30kg/m2

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Skin allergy, including eczema or allergic contact dermatitis in device placement area
2. Diagnosed heart condition or cardiovascular disease
3. Cardiovascular event in the previous 2 months
4. Implanted medical devices including cardioverter defibrillator and pacemaker
5. Previous or current cardiac arrhythmia
6. Autonomic neuropathy
7. Neuromuscular disease
8. Diagnosed epilepsy or recurrent seizures
9. Hypertension (\>140/90 mmHg)
10. Hypotension (\<95/65 mmHg)
11. Metal work in the head or neck, excluding dental fillings
12. Current migraine
13. Pregnancy
14. Diagnosed or suspected deep vein thrombosis within previous 2 months
15. Recent cancer diagnosis or cancerous legions in proximity to device placement area
16. Alcohol dependence
17. Recent infection requiring hospital admission or medical treatment within the previous month, including leprosy
18. Swollen, inflamed, infected, or broken skin in device placement area
19. Recent surgery within 10 months in, or near, device placement area
20. Currently taking medications, excluding contraceptive medication
21. Long facial hair in device placement area
